ui.newcomerLead: You do not need prior knowledge or a special feeling. This is a calm practice of noticing your body, breath and attention.
ui.newcomerReassurance: There is no right way to experience this. Keep what feels useful, and let the rest pass by.
ui.newcomerCentresTitle: The seven centres, in simple words
ui.newcomerCentresNote: “Chakra” is a traditional map for reflection. These are prompts for attention, not medical facts or something you must feel.
ui.newcomerCrown: meaning, openness and the wider picture
ui.newcomerControls: The guide will speak, music may play, and there can be quiet pauses. You can pause, adjust Journey Tuning, or stop at any time. Sit or lie down comfortably and breathe naturally.
ui.newcomerBodyMap: A simple attention map: from the base of the spine to the crown of the head.
ui.newcomerOrientationIntro: Chakra means wheel in Sanskrit. In this traditional practice, the seven chakras form a map of attention along the centre line of the body. We will meet them one at a time, from the base of the spine to the crown of the head.
ui.newcomerRootNarration: Root sits at the base of the spine. It brings steadiness and the feeling of solid ground beneath you.
ui.newcomerSacralNarration: Sacral sits in the lower belly. It brings ease, creativity, and simple joy.
ui.newcomerSolarNarration: Solar Plexus sits in the upper belly. It brings confidence, clear choices, and steady energy.
ui.newcomerHeartNarration: Heart sits at the centre of the chest. It brings care, kindness, and warm connection.
ui.newcomerThroatNarration: Throat sits at the throat. It brings clear expression and calm listening.
ui.newcomerThirdEyeNarration: Third Eye sits at the centre of the forehead. It brings focus, insight, and a clear view of your life.
ui.newcomerCrownNarration: Crown sits at the top of the head. It brings peace, openness, and a wider view.
ui.newcomerOrientationClosing: These are traditional symbols for reflection and focus. Simply follow the centres you selected, at your own ease, and let the practice work gently.
ui.newcomerGuidedStatus: A short guided orientation is playing…
ui.newcomerGuidedNarration: Chakra means wheel in Sanskrit. In this traditional practice, the seven chakras are a simple map for attention along the centre of the body, from the base of the spine to the crown of the head. On the figure, Root is at the base of the spine; Sacral is in the lower abdomen; Solar is in the upper abdomen; Heart is at the centre of the chest; Throat is in the throat area; Third Eye is at the centre of the forehead; and Crown is at the top of the head. Root can be a prompt for steadiness. Sacral for feeling and creativity. Solar for choice and confidence. Heart for care and connection. Throat for expression. Third Eye for reflection. Crown for meaning and openness. You do not need to feel anything special or make anything happen. We will move gently through the centres you selected, using breath, imagery, sound, and quiet pauses as invitations for your attention.

ui.dharanaFocusGuidance: Let your attention rest only on this anchor. Everything else softens into the background. When the mind wanders, gently return to this one clear point.
ui.dharanaClosing: Now let the anchor soften. Relax your gaze and let your awareness widen again. Notice your breath, your body, and the space around you. Carry this steadiness into what comes next.
ui.visualizationFocusPrompt: Choose an experience, a possibility, or a direction to explore in your mind.
ui.dharanaGuidance: Let your attention rest only on this anchor. Allow everything else to soften into the background. When the mind wanders, notice gently and return to this one clear point.
ui.visualizationGuidance: Let your eyes gently shut. Let that experience become a simple scene in your inner mind. Notice where you are, what you see and hear, and how your body feels. Notice how you respond. Let the scene grow clear and familiar, all on its own.
ui.visualizationReturn: Now let the scene soften. Slowly open your eyes when you are ready, and bring its calm clarity with you.
ui.visualizationSilenceWakePrompt: As this quiet practice comes to an end, begin to notice your breath and the space around you. Return slowly and calmly.
ui.bodyScanOpening: Let your eyes gently shut. Let your body rest, fully supported. We will move awareness slowly from the top of the head down to the toes. Notice each sensation, each tension, and each quiet place, just as it is. Pass gently over any area that feels uncomfortable, and keep moving.
bodyScanRegions: Bring awareness to the top of your head and scalp. Notice warmth, tingling, or a simple quiet.
Notice your forehead and eyes, then your cheeks and jaw. Let each sensation rest as it is, and let the face soften.
Move awareness through your neck and shoulders, down your arms to your fingertips. Notice where the body feels light, heavy, or open.
Notice your chest and upper back, and the natural rise and fall of your breath. Let the breath move freely on its own.
Bring awareness to your belly, lower back, and pelvis. Feel the sensations here with patience and kindness.
Move through your thighs and knees. Notice contact, temperature, or a quiet stillness.
Continue through your lower legs and ankles, noticing whatever is present with calm acceptance.
Finally, feel your feet, heels, and every toe. Sense their contact with the ground or the support beneath you.
ui.bodyScanClosing: Now sense your whole body as one complete field, from the top of your head to the tips of your toes. Feel the support beneath you. Your body is at ease, just as it is. This grounded awareness stays with you as the journey continues.
ui.notingOpening: Now notice whatever experience is strongest. Give it one quiet, simple label in your mind, such as thinking, hearing, or warmth. Then release the label and wait. Thoughts and feelings come and go on their own, and you simply watch. If anything feels overwhelming, return to the feeling of your breath.
notingReminders: Notice what is here now. Name it gently, then let the word go.
A repeated thought can simply be labelled thinking again. This is part of the practice.
If an emotion is strong, use a simple label such as sadness, fear, or just feeling. Name it and let it be.
If no label seems right, quietly use the word knowing, or return to your breath. Any simple word works.
ui.notingClosing: Now let all labels fall away. Notice the quiet awareness in which thoughts, sounds, emotions, and sensations appear and pass. Carry this clear, spacious attention into the next part of the journey.
ui.undoUnlearnSubtitle: A private practice of acknowledgement, forgiveness, and release.
ui.undoUnlearnOpening: Simply rest with your breath. Your mind can stay quiet and open. Whatever no longer supports you loosens in its own time. Your breath is always here as an anchor. You are free to end this practice whenever you choose.
undoUnlearnPhases: Every person carries learned habits and unfinished experiences. Acknowledge this gently, with no memory to search for and no story to build.
Let any part of you that is ready receive self-forgiveness, gently. Self-forgiveness keeps your responsibility and frees you from extra weight.

If forgiveness from another person matters to you, quietly pray for forgiveness. No one needs to be pictured, named, or contacted. Their response, safety, and freedom of choice remain entirely their own.
If forgiveness towards someone else is right for you today, allow as much as feels safe. Forgiveness is not approval, and it is not permission for harm.
Let earlier parts of you receive kindness, without revisiting what they lived through. You did your best with the awareness you had at the time. Offer yourself care now.
Picture a compassionate witness beside you. This witness reminds you that true responsibility never asks for endless self-punishment.
Soften your effort. Let your jaw, shoulders, and hands let go of holding. Your breathing becomes easy. Release what is ready to go, gently and naturally.
Rest in the quiet that follows. Keep what supports you. What no longer serves you grows lighter and lighter in its own time.
ui.undoUnlearnClosing: Keep the understanding that serves you. Hold on to your responsibility and your freedom of choice. Move forward lightly, and trust the quiet work of this practice.

ui.quietCourageSubtitle: A private, gentle practice for exploring authentic expression at your own pace.
ui.quietCourageOpening: Settle into the support beneath you. This is a private space for your own quiet strength. Keep everything to yourself, imagine a simple everyday situation, or rest with your breath. Your courage grows in its own way, at your own pace.
quietCouragePhases: Notice a wish, a boundary, or a way of being you would like to make room for. Even a small or unclear feeling is a good beginning. Keep it private, and let it rest gently in your awareness.
Imagine a safe, ordinary moment where you choose to express something. Keep it light and simple, an imagined scene that stays private and involves only you.
Imagine taking one small step at your own pace. You can pause, wait, or set a boundary. Courage includes protecting your comfort.
Notice what helps you feel steady and supported. You stay fully yourself, and this quiet strength stays with you. Take what serves you.
ui.quietCourageClosing: Let the imagined moment soften. Notice your breath, the support beneath you, and the room around you. Your choices are your own. Return gently, at your own pace.
ui.confidenceVisualizationSubtitle: A gentle, fully clothed practice in self-kindness and confidence. No appearance goal or action is required.
ui.confidenceVisualizationOpening: Settle comfortably. Imagine yourself in a familiar, peaceful place, fully dressed and at ease. Here you are accepted exactly as you are.
confidenceVisualizationSteps: Notice one quality or strength you appreciate in yourself. Even a quiet, ordinary quality has real value.
Picture yourself in a small everyday moment with that quality beside you. Confidence means being gently on your own side, with nothing to perform.
Let the image soften. Keep what you imagined that serves you. Rest with one natural breath.
ui.confidenceVisualizationClosing: Let the scene fade at its own pace. Feel the support beneath you and return to the room. You are enough, just as you are.

ui.ctSafetyNote: Before you play, the receiver marks every body place Yes, Maybe or No in private. The game never picks a No. The Pause button is always on the screen.

ui.eyeShooterNote: A gaze game for two. Look, hold, blink — and score.
ui.esWhat: A no-touch practice game for people who find it hard to look at someone. Sit face to face with your partner. You use only your eyes.
ui.esStep1: Pick a spot on your partner from the points table below.
ui.esStep2: Look at that spot and hold your focus for {{seconds}} seconds.
ui.esStep3: Blink once. That is your shot — add its points.
ui.esStep4: Keep going until you reach your goal. Harder spots give more points.
ui.esGoalTitle: How much do you want to play?
ui.esGoalNote: Goal: {{points}} points. Keep the score in your head or say it aloud.
ui.esTips: Go slowly. If it feels too much, look away, breathe, and try an easier spot.
ui.esPartner: Play only with a partner who agrees. Nothing is recorded or saved.

ui.pitchSubtitle: Choose your feeling. A short guided session — just a voice and soft music.
ui.pitchInviteText: Imagine what 20 minutes could do for you.
ui.pitch_calm_opening: Welcome. For the next two minutes, this time is just for you. Whether you are sitting or standing, get comfortable and let your shoulders drop.
pitch_calm_steps: Breathe in slowly through your nose, and let it out gently through your mouth.
Once more. Breathe in, and breathe out a little longer. Feel your body soften.
Notice your feet on the ground and the support beneath you. Everything is steady right now.
Bring one calm thought to mind: I can take this moment slowly.
ui.pitch_calm_closing: Take one last easy breath. Carry this calm with you as you look around the room.
ui.pitch_courage_opening: Welcome. Let's spend two minutes building quiet strength. Sit or stand tall, with your feet steady on the ground.
pitch_courage_steps: Lift your chest a little and relax your shoulders. Notice how steady you already are.
Take a strong breath in, hold it for a moment, and let it go with a slow breath out.
Think of one time you handled something hard. You got through it.
Say it quietly in your mind: I can handle today, one step at a time.
ui.pitch_courage_closing: Take one more strong breath. Keep this tall, steady feeling as you get back to your day.
ui.pitch_energy_opening: Welcome. Here are two minutes to wake up your body and mind. Sit or stand tall, and let's begin.
pitch_energy_steps: Take three short breaths in through your nose, and one long breath out. In, in, in, and out. Go at a comfortable pace.
Once more. In, in, in, and out. If you feel light-headed, just breathe normally.
Roll your shoulders back twice, and stretch your arms up high.
Now bring a small smile to your face. Notice how that feels.
ui.pitch_energy_closing: One last deep breath in, and out. You are awake, fresh, and ready to go.
ui.pitch_focus_opening: Welcome. Let's use two minutes to clear your mind. Sitting or standing, get comfortable and rest your eyes on one point.
pitch_focus_steps: Breathe in and count one, breathe out. Breathe in and count two, breathe out. Breathe in and count three, breathe out.
If a thought comes, simply notice it, and come back to your breath.
Now choose one thing you want to do next. Just one.
See yourself starting it, calm and clear. One thing at a time.
ui.pitch_focus_closing: Take one more breath, and keep this clear mind as you begin.
